rca of the issue: Reported bug: 'already exists' on old emails after fork and Google sign-up logging into old customer id. RCA: Forked environment inherited OLD MongoDB (users, user_sessions, email_verifications, counters) while backend was repointed to NEW Google Sheets. The duplicate-email guard in auth/service.py queries Mongo, which still had the old user rows -> false positive 'already exists'; Google sign-in matched the same old Mongo user -> old customer_no returned. Mitigation applied by main agent: wiped the above collections and restarted backend; the seed user CUST-000000 is re-created idempotently. Verification in this iteration: (a) brand-new emails and the specific old-env email rajib_sengupta@yahoo.com both now get a fresh verification link (no false 'already exists'); (b) first fresh registration lands in NEW customer_master as CUST-000001 and series increments to 2; (c) duplicate guards still work for genuine duplicates (same email, same mobile).
